transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Collins (Redwood AE), Ravi Menon (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (Larkwell CISO), Ethan Park (Head of Cloud), Nadia Li (Compliance Manager)

[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jamie from Redwood, ravi and i will run through our SOC 2/ISO posture and answer any ques- questions, um, about Trust Center, controls mapping, KMS.
[00:12] Maria: Great, thanks. We're doing a vendor posture review for Larkwell's infosec board next week, need to confirm Redwood's controls and whether we can get the actual reports.
[00:25] Ravi: Totally. We'll cover where the reports live, what the scope is, and how the controls map to common frameworks. Quick note: sometimes the auto-transcript will say "Redwood Inference" as "Redwood inference" or "readout"—ignore those typos.
[00:40] Ethan: First question: do you provide SOC 2 Type II? And is the ISO scope including hosting and processing of PHI?
[00:49] Jamie: Yes, we have a SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificate. The SOC 2 scope covers our hosted API and dedicated deployments; ISO covers our control plane and datacenter-level controls. For PHI, we have controls and BAAs available—we do support BAA for enterprise customers.
[01:05] Maria: Do you share the full report or a redacted version? We need evidence for section 3.
[01:12] Ravi: We typically provide a redacted SOC 2 report to prospective customers over the Trust Center portal. For customers under contract we can provide more detailed evidence under NDA; also we can grant read-only Trust Center access for audit purposes.
[01:30] Nadia: What's the process to get read-only access? We've got a compliance window the week of the 14th.
[01:38] Jamie: We can provision read-only Trust Center access — needs a list of users and their emails, and a short SSO/SCIM setup. We can get it done in 2-3 business days typically.
[01:50] Ethan: about SSO, we use Okta with SCIM. What's your support for provisioning and RBAC?
[01:58] Ravi: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning; RBAC is role-based with admin/engineer/read-only roles. SCIM provisioning maps groups to roles, though there are a few small caveats in older versions — we'll send the exact attribute mappings.
[02:15] Maria: How granular is the RBAC? We need ability to restrict access to logs and billing separately.
[02:20] Ravi: Good question. Right now roles separate console admin vs. operator vs readonly. Billing access is separate — it's tied to account-level permissions. We can do custom roles for enterprise private deployments; on hosted tenants we have a standard set but can approximate via groups.
[02:40] Nadia: Audit logs: retention, who can access them, and are they tamper-evident?
[02:46] Jamie: Audit logs are stored for 13 months by default for enterprise customers, with options for longer retention as an add-on. Logs are immutable and stored with integrity checks; we can provide hash verification for specific artifacts if needed.
[03:05] Ethan: Are audit logs accessible from the Trust Center or do we need an API?
[03:10] Ravi: Logs dump is available via the console and via an API; we also can push to a customer's SIEM via syslog or forward to a GCS/S3 bucket. For private deployments we can ship logs directly into the customer's logging pipeline.
[03:26] Maria: Encryption at rest? Customer-managed keys? KMS?
[03:30] Jamie: We encrypt data at rest and in transit. For hosted we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS or GCP KMS depending on region; for dedicated/private we can integrate with on-prem HSMs. We should verify the exact key lifecycle you require.
[03:53] Nadia: We need to ensure tokenization/PII redaction in logs. How's that handled?
[03:58] Ravi: Redwood can redact PII from logs; by default sensitive outputs are not stored in the request logs beyond metadata, and payload-level retention is configurable. There are also disposable keys and options to exclude raw payloads from long-term storage — we'll capture the exact options in the controls mapping doc.
[04:20] Ethan: On data residency — we process in region eu-west-1 for our EU customers, but does Redwood guarantee in-region processing and storage for hosted customers?
[04:29] Jamie: Yes, we offer regional tenancy; you can pin region in the project settings — however some ancillary services (like analytics) may be aggregated in the control plane depending on plan. We'll share the data flow diagram.
[04:46] Maria: Controls mapping — do you have a pre-built mapping to SOC 2/ISO controls?
[04:51] Ravi: Yes, we maintain a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, ISO 27001 Annex A controls, and common healthcare frameworks like HITRUST. We'll send the spreadsheet and a redaction guide.
[05:05] Nadia: For evidence, we need sample procedures and where to find evidence in Trust Center.
[05:12] Jamie: Trust Center exposes the evidence inventory and link to artifacts. For some items we provide screenshots and for others we can provide extracts under NDA. We'll list owner contacts in the mapping doc.
[05:28] Maria: Regarding BAAs and PHI — you mentioned support, what's the SLA for data deletion requests?
[05:35] Ravi: We have documented data retention and deletion procedures; typical deletion completion is within 7 days for ephemeral caches and up to 30 days for backups depending on provider retention windows — we'll include the timeline in the controls doc.
[05:55] Ethan: Any competitor differences — we use ProviderX for some infra and they keep logs for 26 months, is that an issue?
[06:03] Jamie: Our default is 13 months but we can extend retention or set up a copy to your archive bucket to match 26 months. For dedicated/private we can match your retention policy.
[06:18] Maria: Can you show where the ISO certificate is — I want to confirm scope and expiration.
[06:23] Jamie: Yes, we'll send the certificate link; expiration is 2027-04-30 and scope includes core platform services.
[06:30] Nadia: On encryption in transit — do you provide mTLS for service-to-service?
[06:35] Ravi: We use TLS 1.2+ internally and can enable mTLS for private endpoints. For hosted API we rely on TLS + token auth; for dedicated/private we can enable mTLS between services upon request.
[06:50] Ethan: For KMS and bring-your-own-key, what does key rotation look like? Any downtime risk?
[06:57] Jamie: Key rotation is seamless when using cloud KMS — we support key versions and automatic rotation; we'll walk through our KMS integration in the deep dive and provide sample rotation playbooks. There's typically no downtime.
[07:15] Maria: About RBAC: we need attribute-based access controls for certain features — is that supported?
[07:21] Ravi: Not full ABAC today; we have group-based RBAC and can tie into SCIM attributes. For enterprise private installs we can add more granular controls to meet requirements — will note as a customization.
[07:40] Nadia: Evidence owners — can you provide contacts for compliance items?
[07:44] Jamie: Yes, we'll add point-of-contact names and emails in the controls mapping doc; for audit access it's typically our compliance team (compliance@redwood.ai) and SE for technical artifacts.
[07:58] Ethan: Are change logs and deployment history part of the artifact set? Our auditors ask for deployment evidence.
[08:05] Ravi: Yes, we can provide deployment history, change approvals, and CI pipeline audit trails for enterprise customers; these are captured in the Trust Center as well or exported on request.
[08:22] Maria: Any pen testing results?
[08:25] Jamie: We run annual external penetration tests and internal pentests; summary reports can be shared, full reports under NDA.
[08:35] Nadia: For legal, we have to ensure indemnity language — I assume your BAAs cover that but legal will follow up.
[08:42] Jamie: Yep, legal will handle contract language; we'll share standard BAA and security addendum.
[08:50] Ethan: Ok, next steps?
[08:52] Jamie: Recap: we'll send SOC 2 Type II redacted, ISO cert link, controls mapping spreadsheet, provision Trust Center read-only access if you send user list, and schedule technical deep dive on SSO/KMS.
[09:05] Maria: Timeline — can you get this by Friday?
[09:08] Jamie: We'll aim for Friday (2026-12-11).
[09:12] Nadia: I'll send the list of users and sample SAML metadata by tomorrow.
[09:17] Ethan: I'll compile evidence owner list and send before 2026-12-12.
[09:23] Jamie: Great. Thanks everyone.

Action items (captured in transcript): Jamie to send SOC2/ISO links; Ravi to send controls mapping and attribute mappings for SCIM; Customer to send user list and evidence owner list.

End of transcript. Notes: minor transcription errors where product terms like "KV cache" became "K V cache" and "Trust Center" sometimes transcribed as "trust center portal".
